source.author: verg
source.text: Tum Iuno omnipotens, longum miserata dolorem difficilisque obitus, Irim demisit Olympo, quae luctantem animam nexosque resolveret artus.
source.text_original: Tum Iuno omnipotens, longum miserata dolorem / difficilisque obitus, Irim demisit Olympo, / quae luctantem animam nexosque resolveret artus.
source.text_english: Then almighty Juno, pitying their long suffering and hard death, sent Iris down from Olympus, to loosen the struggling soul and the bound limbs.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: tandem animi incertum confusaque pectora firmat relligio, tendensque pias ad sidera palmas omnipotens regina, inquit quam, turbidus atro aethere caeruleum quateret cum Iuppiter imbrem, ipse ego praecipiti tumidum per Enipea nimbo in campos et tuta tuli nec credere quivi ante deam, quam te tonitru nutuque reposci coniugis et subita raptam formidine vidi, da Scythiam Phasimque mihi; tuque, innuba Pallas, eripe me.
reuse.text_original: tandem animi incertum confusaque pectora firmat / relligio, tendensque pias ad sidera palmas / 'omnipotens regina', inquit 'quam, turbidus atro / aethere caeruleum quateret cum Iuppiter imbrem, / ipse ego praecipiti tumidum per Enipea nimbo / in campos et tuta tuli nec credere quivi / ante deam, quam te tonitru nutuque reposci / coniugis et subita raptam formidine vidi, / da Scythiam Phasimque mihi; tuque, innuba Pallas, / eripe me.
reuse.text_english: At last religion steadies their wavering minds and troubled hearts; and the all-powerful queen, stretching her pious hands to the stars, said: when, from the dark sky, angry Jupiter was shaking down the blue rain, I myself then, through the rushing flood of Enipeus, carried the swollen stream into the fields and to safety, nor could I believe it before the goddess, until I saw you reclaimed by thunder and by your husband’s command, and snatched away in sudden fear. Grant me Scythia and Phasis; and you too, unwedded Pallas, rescue me.
